channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: United States: Bifurcated revival with advanced sectors – ING
item.description: ING’s James Knightley and Coco Zhang argue that US manufacturing is finally reviving after years of stagnation, helped by reshoring narratives, AI-driven investment and defence spending.

item.title: US Dollar: Fed resilience supports gains – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad highlights that the Dollar is advancing broadly as a hawkish Federal Reserve stance combines with strong US economic outperformance.

item.title: Fed's Paulson warns more hikes possible as inflation fight hardens
item.description: Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson crossed the wires on Thursday, signaling that further rate hikes may be needed to lower inflation. She acknowledged that the rate hike in September helped to “move policy to better inflation-fighting posture.”

item.title: Gold bears tighten their grip as Fed rate hike bets rise
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) slides to a one-week low on Thursday as rising US Treasury yields and a stronger US Dollar (USD) reflect an increasingly hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) outlook. At the time of writing, XAU/USD trades around $4,263, down nearly 0.54% on the day.

item.title: Euro hovers near two-month low as hawkish Fed outlook weighs
item.description: EUR/USD hovers near a two-month low on Thursday as expectations of another Federal Reserve (Fed) interest-rate hike keep the US Dollar (USD) firmly supported. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 1.1372, remaining on the back foot for a fourth consecutive day.

item.title: Australian Dollar remains under pressure despite stronger-than-expected jobs data
item.description: AUD/USD trims its losses on Thursday and trades around 0.7030 at the time of writing, down 0.15% on the day.

item.title: “You can’t wait too long”: BoE’s Breeden warns on rate hikes amid energy shock
item.description: Bank of England (BoE) Deputy Governor Sarah Breeden said on Thursday that it is “not at all obvious” that there is a path toward lower energy prices, according to Reuters.

item.title: Euro: Weak as Fed credibility supports Dollar near term – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Thu Lan Nguyen argues that the unanimous Federal Reserve rate hike has temporarily restored its credibility and supported the Dollar, prompting a cut in the EUR/USD year-end forecast to 1.15 from 1.17.

item.title: Canada: Revised demographics reshape growth view – RBC
item.description: Royal Bank of Canada economist Rachel Battaglia explains that Statistics Canada’s upward revision to population data has erased earlier signs of negative growth and now shows Canada’s population rising 0.5% year-over-year in Q2.

item.title: Fed’s Hammack warns persistent inflation could make return to target harder
item.description: Cleveland Federal Reserve (Fed) President Beth Hammack warned on Thursday that inflation remains elevated in the United States (US), stressing that persistent price pressures could make the Fed’s task increasingly difficult.

item.title: Germany: Cyclical resilience versus structural risks – ING
item.description: ING’s Carsten Brzeski highlights that Germany’s IFO index has risen for five consecutive months, pointing to a cyclical rebound and unexpected resilience in the German economy.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: RSI nears overbought territory as bulls remain in control
item.description: USD/CHF climbs to its highest level since May 2025 on Thursday as the Swiss Franc (CHF) weakens across the board following the Swiss National Bank’s (SNB) decision to leave its policy rate unchanged at 0%.

item.title: Euro: Downside risks for EUR against US Dollar – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley discusses EUR/USD trading near its yearly lows despite consensus forecasts that had expected the pair around 1.18–1.20 in late 2026.

item.title: Silver price falls as Fed hawkish outlook drives US yields higher
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) extends its decline on Thursday, falling 1.23% to trade around $63.65 at the time of writing. The precious metal comes under heavy selling pressure as increasingly hawkish expectations surrounding the Federal Reserve (Fed) push United States (US) Treasury yields sharply higher.

item.title: Swedish Krona: Riksbank hawkish hold backs currency – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad reports the Swedish Krona (SEK) rallied after the Riksbank delivered a hawkish hold, keeping rates unchanged but signaling more tightening ahead.

item.title: US Initial Jobless Claims dropped to 197K last week
item.description: According to a report from the US Department of Labour (DOL) released on Thursday, the number of US citizens submitting new applications for unemployment insurance decreased to 197K for the week ending September 19.

item.title: Japanese Yen weakness lifts British Pound as wide interest-rate gap bites
item.description: GBP/JPY rebounds on Thursday, supported mainly by broad-based weakness in the Japanese Yen (JPY) rather than strength in the British Pound (GBP), as traders assess the monetary policy outlooks of the Bank of Japan (BoJ) and the Bank of England (BoE).

item.title: Reserve Bank of Australia: September hike case and path – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Macro Research team, led by Prashant Newnaha and Howard Du, expects the Reserve Bank of Australia to raise the cash rate by 25bps to 4.60% at the September meeting.

item.title: Norges Bank: Policy rate seen elevated for longer – Nordea
item.description: Nordea’s Kjetil Olsen notes that Norges Bank raised its policy rate by 25bp to 4.5% and lifted the policy rate path, implying some risk of a further hike over the next six months.

item.title: Bank of Canada: Energy risks complicate October decision - RBC
item.description: Rachel Battaglia at Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) argues that higher backward-looking population growth implies stronger potential output, mechanically reducing pressure on the Bank of Canada (BoC) to hike rates.

item.title: Indian Rupee declines significantly due to oil price recovery, surging US yields
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) extends its losses against the US Dollar (USD) on Thursday.

item.title: Canadian Dollar dips to fresh two-month lows amid higher US yields, Fed hiking bets
item.description: The Canadian Dollar (CAD) extends losses for the fourth consecutive day against the US Dollar (USD) on Thursday, as surging US Treasury yields and rising bets of Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hikes are propelling the Greenback across the board.

item.title: US President Trump: Super Intelligence will be a big topic of discussion
item.description: United States (US) President Donald Trump shares excitement ahead of meeting with Chinese leader Xi Jinping through a post on Truth.Social.

item.title: Euro advances as strong German IFO, cautious BoJ outlook weigh on Japanese Yen
item.description: EUR/JPY trades higher around 180.55 on Thursday, gaining 0.19% on the day at the time of writing.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Labor data underpins RBA hike view – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad observes AUD/USD trading near its 200-day moving average support as broad Dollar strength weighs on the pair.

item.title: British Pound sees more downside as US Yields rally further
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) is down 0.12% to near 1.3225 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Thursday.

item.title: US yields jump to multi-year highs on Fed tightening bets, bond market turmoil
item.description: US Treasury yields stretched to their highest levels in years on Wednesday, fuelled by a mix of rising expectations of further monetary tightening by the US Federal Reserve (Fed), following upbeat US business activity data and a poor US Treasury bond auction.

item.title: BoE’s Dhingra says financial conditions have already done much of the tightening
item.description: Bank of England (BoE) Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) member Swati Dhingra struck a dovish tone on Thursday, highlighting signs of easing price pressures and weakness in the United Kingdom (UK) labour market, according to Reuters.

item.title: Mexican Peso: Downward momentum returns after 200-DMA break – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale analysts, including Kenneth Broux, note that USD/MXN has broken above a multi-month descending trend line and reclaimed its 200-day moving average for the first time since April 2025.

item.title: PBoC vows to maintain loose monetary policy, keep Chinese Yuan stable
item.description: The People’s Bank of China (PBoC) said on Thursday that it will step up counter-cyclical adjustments and continue to implement an “appropriately loose” monetary policy, according to Reuters.
